mainTopic: The ברייתא of רבי זכאי comparing שבת to other מצוות, and why רבי יוחנן rejected it
overview: רבי זכאי taught a ברייתא before רבי יוחנן saying שבת is stricter than other מצוות in one way, and other מצוות are stricter than שבת in another. The גמרא first tests the שבת side. Two different acts bring two חטאות everywhere, and the same act repeated brings one חטאת everywhere, so no difference appears. That explains why רבי יוחנן sent the ברייתא outside. The גמרא then suggests that 'other מצוות' means עבודה זרה, where רבי אמי says several acts in one lapse bring only one חטאת. But the second half of the ברייתא needs a case of שוגג בלא מתכוין in עבודה זרה. Every case tried fails: love or fear does not work for רבא, and 'thinks it is permitted' does not work for שבת. Next the גמרא suggests splitting the ברייתא, with the first half about עבודה זרה and the second half about ordinary מצוות, backed by שמואל's rule about a מתעסק. רבי יוחנן rejects this kind of split, as his statement about the barrel משנה shows. The גמרא then turns back to רבי אמי's statement itself, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא: how שבת is stricter than other מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכאי's ברייתא says each of the two areas has a stringency. On שבת, two מלאכות done in one lapse of awareness bring a חטאת for each one, and this is not so for other מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he taught before him: שבת is stricter than other מצוות in one way, and other מצוות are stricter than שבת in another way. The stringency of שבת: if a person did two acts in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each one. That is not so for other מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the exact ברייתא that רבי זכאי taught before רבי יוחנן. This step gives the first half: the way שבת is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up a two-sided comparison. Its first claim is about counting חטאות: on שבת, two acts done in one העלם אחד bring two חטאות, while for other מצוות they supposedly do not. The rest of our text will test whether this claim really holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency, a way in which one law is stricter
Other מצוות (other prohibitions besides שבת)
One lapse of awareness: all the acts were done during a single period of forgetting
Liable, here meaning obligated to bring a חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: Everything here is about mistakes (שוגג), not sins done on purpose. The question is how many חטאת offerings a person brings.

phrases.english: This is what he taught before him:
phrases.notes: This continues from earlier on the דף, where רבי זכאי taught this ברייתא in front of רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: There is a stringency in Shabbat over other מצוות,
and a stringency in other מצוות over Shabbat.
The stringency of Shabbat:
that regarding Shabbat, if he did two acts in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable for each and every one,
which is not so with other מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the text by quoting רבי זכאי's ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, two acts in one העלם אחד bring a חטאת for each act. The ברייתא claims this is not so for other מצוות.

steps.title: The ברייתא: how other מצוות are stricter than שבת
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the ברייתא says that for other מצוות, someone who sinned by mistake without intending the act at all is still liable, but on שבת he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stringency of other מצוות: with other מצוות, if he sinned by mistake without intending the act, he is liable. That is not so on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its comparison by giving the way other מצוות are stricter than שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different kind of mistake: the person did not even mean to do the act he ended up doing. For other מצוות he still brings a חטאת, but on שבת he does not. The גמרא later uses this half to reject reading the ברייתא as being about עבודה זרה (step 8), and then explains it with concrete cases (step 15).

keyTerms.meaning: Sinned by mistake (unknowingly)
Without intending to do the act at all

phrases.english: The stringency of other מצוות:
that with other מצוות,
if he sinned by mistake without intending the act, he is liable,
which is not so with Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided comparison begun in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For other מצוות, a mistaken act done without intending the act still brings a חטאת. On שבת it does not.

steps.title: What case does the שבת stringency mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first claim of the ברייתא and asks what exact case it is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'The stringency of שבת is that if he did two acts...' What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first half of the ברייתא and asks for the exact case. This question sets up the test that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To check whether שבת really differs from other מצוות, we need to know which 'two acts' the ברייתא means. The next steps try out the two possible cases.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: חוֹמֶר בַּשַּׁבָּת, שֶׁהַשַּׁבָּת עָשָׂה שְׁתַּיִם כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: The stringency of Shabbat: that regarding Shabbat, if he did two acts, etc.
phrases.notes: כו׳ means 'and so on.' The גמרא is pointing back to the full line we saw in step 1.

phrases.english: What is the case?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: חוֹמֶר בַּשַּׁבָּת, שֶׁהַשַּׁבָּת עָשָׂה שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the first claim of the ברייתא for analysis
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of 'two acts in one העלם' makes שבת stricter than other מצוות?

steps.title: Two different acts: no difference
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the case is two different מלאכות, such as קצירה and טחינה. The matching case for other מצוות is eating חלב and דם, and there he also brings two חטאות. So there is no stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he did reaping and grinding, the matching case with other מצוות is eating forbidden fat and blood. Here he is liable twice, and there he is liable twice!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible case, two different kinds of מלאכה, and shows that it gives no difference between שבת and other מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קצירה and טחינה are two separate מלאכות, so he brings two חטאות. But eating חלב and דם breaks two separate prohibitions, so there too he brings two חטאות. Since both sides are the same, this case cannot be the 'stringency' the ברייתא describes.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Reaping and grinding, two different מלאכות
The matching case, the parallel
Forbidden fat and blood, two different prohibitions
Two (here, two חטאות)

phrases.english: If you say that he did reaping and grinding,
the matching case with other מצוות
is where he ate forbidden fat and blood.
Here he is liable for two,
and here he is liable for two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the first answer to the question of step 3 and knocks it down
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that שבת is stricter in counting חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two different acts bring two חטאות both on שבת and with other מצוות, so this case shows no stringency.

steps.title: The same act twice: still no difference
steps.stepSummary: The other possibility is repeating the same act: eating חלב twice, or doing קצירה twice on שבת. In both cases only one חטאת is brought, so again there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, with other מצוות, where he is liable only once, what is the case? Where he ate forbidden fat and again forbidden fat. The matching case on שבת is where he reaped and reaped again. Here he is liable once, and there he is liable once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the opposite case, the same act repeated, and shows that it also gives no difference between שבת and other מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With other מצוות, a person brings one חטאת only when he repeats the same sin, like eating חלב twice. The matching שבת case is doing קצירה twice, and there too he brings only one חטאת. So neither possible case shows that שבת is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (switches to a new possibility)
Forbidden fat and again forbidden fat: the same sin twice
Reaping and again reaping: the same מלאכה twice
One (one חטאת)

steps.whatToRemember: Different acts bring two חטאות both on שבת and with other מצוות. The same act repeated brings one חטאת in both places. So the first half of the ברייתא shows no real difference.

phrases.english: Rather, with other מצוות,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: where he is liable only once, what is the case?
Where he ate forbidden fat and again forbidden fat.
phrases.notes: Both eatings happened during the same one lapse of awareness.

phrases.english: The matching case with Shabbat
is where he reaped and reaped again.
Here he is liable for one,
and here he is liable for one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, גַּבֵּי שְׁאָר מִצְוֹת דְּאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the only other possible case after step 4 failed, and knocks it down too
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that שבת is stricter in counting חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repeating the same act brings one חטאת both on שבת and with other מצוות, so this case shows no stringency either.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן sent the ברייתא outside
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא's comparison does not work, the גמרא explains that this is why רבי יוחנן told רבי זכאי to go teach it outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is why he said to him: 'Go out and teach it outside!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up by saying the problem it just found is the reason רבי יוחנן rejected רבי זכאי's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4 and 5 showed that the claimed stringency of שבת does not exist in any case. A ברייתא with a comparison that falls apart is not reliable, so רבי יוחנן said it does not belong in the study hall.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is (the reason for) what was said
Go out and teach it outside, meaning this teaching is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן rejected רבי זכאי's ברייתא because its claim that שבת is stricter in counting חטאות turns out to have no real case behind it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא checks a ברייתא: it tests every possible case, and if none of them works, the teaching is set aside.

phrases.english: And this is why he said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן said this to רבי זכאי earlier on the דף.

phrases.english: "Go out and teach it outside!"
phrases.notes: In other words: this teaching doesn't belong in the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the failure of both cases in steps 4 and 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא's claimed stringency of שבת cannot be made to work, which explains why רבי יוחנן rejected it.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא means idol worship, following רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן rejected the ברייתא. It could be about קצירה and טחינה, with 'other מצוות' meaning עבודה זרה, where רבי אמי rules that several acts in one lapse bring only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the problem? Maybe the case really is someone who did קצירה and טחינה on שבת, and 'which is not so with other מצוות' refers to עבודה זרה, following רבי אמי. רבי אמי said: if someone slaughtered, burned incense, and poured a libation to an idol in one lapse of awareness, he brings only one חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rejection of the ברייתא by offering a way to make the comparison work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 failed because חלב and דם also bring two חטאות. But if 'other מצוות' means עבודה זרה, there really is a difference. There, three different acts in one lapse bring only one חטאת, while on שבת two מלאכות bring two. So שבת would truly be stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? (a push-back on an earlier problem)
We have come to idol worship. The ברייתא is read as being about עבודה זרה.
Slaughtered, burned incense, poured a libation (three acts of worship)
One lapse of awareness

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. Here the גמרא keeps the case of two מלאכות on שבת. It only changes what 'other מצוות' means, from all מצוות to עבודה זרה alone.

phrases.english: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps I will actually tell you
that he did reaping and grinding,
and "which is not so with other מצוות"
means we have come to idol worship,
in line with Rabbi Ami,
as Rabbi Ami says:
If he slaughtered, burned incense, and poured a libation
in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּילְמָא לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 6 by offering a new reading that would make the ברייתא work.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rejection of the ברייתא (step 6)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The objection in step 4 assumed 'other מצוות' means all מצוות. If it means only עבודה זרה, where רבי אמי rules that several acts bring one חטאת, then שבת really is stricter.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא does not fit idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא cannot be about עבודה זרה, because its second half says that in other מצוות, שוגג בלא מתכוין is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It cannot be read as being about עבודה זרה. The end of the ברייתא says: other מצוות are stricter, because there someone who sinned by mistake without intending the act at all is still liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idol-worship reading by pointing to the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'other מצוות' means עבודה זרה in the first half, it must mean the same in the second half. That half talks about a person who did the act without intending it at all. The גמרא will next show that this kind of case is hard to find in עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot be set up (this reading does not work)
The last part of a teaching
A stringency (the stricter side)
Sinned by mistake without intending the act at all

phrases.english: It cannot be set up as being about idol worship,
since the last part teaches:
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the ברייתא from step 2.

phrases.english: A stringency in other מצוות,
that in other מצוות,
if he sinned by mistake without intending, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מִיתּוֹקְמָא לֵיהּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, דְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading proposed in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that 'other מצוות' in the ברייתא means עבודה זרה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The second half of the ברייתא needs a case of שוגג בלא מתכוין in 'other מצוות', and that is hard to apply to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: What would an unintended act of idol worship even look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא searches for a case of שוגג בלא מתכוין in עבודה זרה. Bowing to what he thought was a בית הכנסת is fine, because his heart is toward Heaven. Bowing to a statue is either מזיד or nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would a mistaken, unintended act of עבודה זרה look like? If he thought it was a בית הכנסת and bowed, his heart was toward Heaven, so he did nothing wrong. Maybe he saw a statue of a person and bowed to it? If he accepted it as a god, he sinned on purpose. If he did not accept it as a god, his act means nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests possible cases to show why the second half of the ברייתא cannot be about עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each option fails. In the בית הכנסת case he meant to serve ה׳, so there is no sin. In the statue case, either he accepted it as a god, which makes him a מזיד (deliberate sinner) who does not bring a קרבן, or he did not, which means no act of worship happened. Neither gives a שוגג who must bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How would it look?
His heart is toward Heaven
A statue (of a person)
He accepted it upon himself as a god
A deliberate sinner

phrases.english: A mistaken act without intent in idol worship,
what would it look like?
If he thought it was a synagogue
and bowed to it,
his heart was toward Heaven.
Rather, where he saw a statue and bowed to it.

phrases.aramaic: אִי קַבְּלֵיהּ עֲלֵיהּ בֶּאֱלוֹהַּ – מֵזִיד הוּא,
phrases.english: If he accepted it as a god, he is a deliberate sinner,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא קַבְּלֵיהּ עֲלֵיהּ – לֹא כְּלוּם הִיא.
phrases.english: and if he did not accept it, it is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹגֵג בְּלֹא מִתְכַּוֵּין בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the rejection in step 8 by showing that the obvious cases do not work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real case of שוגג בלא מתכוין in עבודה זרה that would require a חטאת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The obvious cases fail: the בית הכנסת case is no sin, and the statue case is either מזיד or no act at all.

steps.title: A possible case: worship out of love or fear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the case could be someone who bowed to an idol out of love or fear of a person, without knowing this is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is someone who bowed out of love or out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers one case that might count as a mistaken act of עבודה זרה. It is setting up the next question about whether this case works for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here he does not accept the idol as a god. He bows because he loves or fears a person, and he does not realize this is forbidden. If that act counts as עבודה זרה, it could be the שוגג case the ברייתא needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Out of love and out of fear (of a person, not of the idol as a god)

phrases.english: Rather, out of love or out of fear.
phrases.notes: He bows because he loves or fears a person, not because he believes in the idol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 with a new case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Worshipping out of love or fear of a person, unaware it is forbidden, could be a mistaken act of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: This case works for אביי but not for רבא
steps.stepSummary: Worship out of love or fear counts as liable according to אביי, but רבא says it is exempt. So for רבא the גמרא still needs a different case, which step 12 offers.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for אביי, who says such a person is liable. But according to רבא, who says he is exempt, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 10, because it only works for one side of an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא argue about someone who bows to an idol out of love or fear. For אביי it counts as עבודה זרה, so a mistaken version would bring a חטאת. For רבא it does not count at all, so there is still no case of שוגג בלא מתכוין in עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one opinion)
What can be said? (the problem is still unsolved)
Exempt

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the עבודה זרה reading of the ברייתא depends on taking אביי's side in his argument with רבא.

phrases.english: This works for Abaye, who says he is liable.
But according to Rava, who says he is exempt,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְאַבַּיֵּי, דְּאָמַר חַיָּיב. אֶלָּא לְרָבָא, דְּאָמַר פָּטוּר, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The love-or-fear case offered in step 10
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבא, worship out of love or fear is exempt, so it cannot be the liable שוגג case the ברייתא needs.

steps.title: A new case: someone who thinks it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is talking about someone who thinks עבודה זרה is permitted. He is liable, but someone who thinks working on שבת is permitted would be completely exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is someone who says it is permitted. That is not so on שבת, where such a person is completely exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: Since love or fear did not work for רבא, the גמרא offers a new case of שוגג in עבודה זרה. It is a person who believes idol worship is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who thinks the whole איסור does not exist is a kind of שוגג. For עבודה זרה he would bring a חטאת. The ברייתא's line 'which is not so on שבת' would then mean that someone who thinks all מלאכה on שבת is permitted is completely פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who thinks the act is permitted, not knowing the prohibition exists at all
Completely exempt, not even bringing a קרבן
Which is not the case; marks a contrast

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he says it is permitted,
phrases.notes: He thinks bowing to the idol is allowed altogether, not just that this one act is okay.

phrases.english: which is not so with שבת,
where he is completely exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the love/fear case that failed for רבא in step 11 with a new case of שוגג in עבודה זרה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is אומר מותר: liable in עבודה זרה, completely exempt on שבת.

steps.title: No one says such a person is fully exempt on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא asked רב נחמן whether someone who forgot both שבת and the מלאכות brings one חטאת or two. No one says he is fully exempt, so the new reading fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן about a lapse of both this and that. He only asked whether to obligate one חטאת or two. That he is completely exempt, no one says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the אומר מותר reading. It shows from רבא's question that a person like this is never totally exempt on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who forgot both that it is שבת and that these מלאכות are forbidden is very close to someone who thinks שבת work is permitted. רבא's only doubt was whether he brings one חטאת or two, so both sides agree he is liable. That contradicts the claim that on שבת he would be פטור לגמרי.

keyTerms.meaning: Unaware of both: that it is שבת, and that the מלאכות are forbidden
To obligate him in one חטאת
Two
There is no one who holds this

phrases.english: He only asked him, up to this point,
רבא of רב נחמן
about a lapse of awareness of this and that:
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means he forgot that it was שבת and also forgot that these kinds of work are forbidden.

phrases.english: only whether to obligate him in one,
or whether to obligate him in two.
Completely exempt? There is no one who says that.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the אומר מותר reading proposed in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that someone who thinks שבת work is permitted is פטור לגמרי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's question assumes such a person is liable and only asks how many חטאות he brings. So no one holds he is fully exempt.

steps.title: Maybe the two halves of the ברייתא talk about different things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the problem was all along. Perhaps the first half of the ברייתא is about עבודה זרה and the second half is about other מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Perhaps I will actually tell you: the first clause is about עבודה זרה, and the last clause is about other מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the rejection in step 8 and asks why the second half of the ברייתא should block the עבודה זרה reading. It suggests the two halves are talking about different subjects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the ברייתא cannot be about עבודה זרה, because its second half speaks of שוגג בלא מתכוין, and no such case worked in עבודה זרה. Now the גמרא says only the first half, about many acts in one lapse, compares שבת to עבודה זרה. The second half, about שוגג בלא מתכוין, compares שבת to ordinary מצוות. That removes the need to find a שוגג בלא מתכוין case in עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? Questions whether there was a real problem
The first clause of a ברייתא or משנה
The last clause
Other מצוות, besides עבודה זרה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Other מצוות' does not mean the same thing in both halves now. In the first half it means עבודה זרה. In the second half it means ordinary מצוות like eating forbidden foods.

phrases.english: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps, actually, I will say to you:
the first clause is about עבודה זרה,
and the last clause is about other מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּלְמָא לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 9 to 13 failed to find a case in עבודה זרה, the גמרא returns to step 8's rejection and questions whether it was a real problem.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא: the two clauses refer to different subjects.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves of the ברייתא must be comparing שבת to the same subject.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא compares שבת to עבודה זרה, and the סיפא compares שבת to ordinary מצוות.

steps.title: What 'unwitting without intent' means in other מצוות
steps.stepSummary: In other מצוות, שוגג בלא מתכוין is someone who swallowed something forbidden thinking it was spittle, and he is liable. On שבת, someone who meant to lift a detached plant and cut an attached one is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'unwitting without intent' means he thought it was spittle and swallowed it. That is not so on שבת, where he is exempt: one who intended to lift something detached and cut something attached is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the split reading by giving clear examples for the second half of the ברייתא. One example is for ordinary מצוות and one is for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ordinary איסורים, eating something forbidden without meaning to eat it at all still brings a חטאת. On שבת, a מלאכה done without intending that act at all is פטור. Lifting a detached plant and accidentally cutting an attached one is that kind of case. This is exactly the stricter point about other מצוות that the סיפא describes.

keyTerms.meaning: Sinned by mistake without even intending the act itself
Spittle
Detached from the ground
Still attached to the ground

steps.whatToRemember: Under the split reading, the רישא of the ברייתא compares שבת to עבודה זרה (many acts in one lapse). The סיפא compares שבת to ordinary מצוות: swallowing something forbidden without meaning to is liable, but a מלאכה on שבת done without meaning to is פטור.

phrases.english: And 'unwitting without intent' means
that he thought it was spittle and swallowed it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is something forbidden in his mouth, like forbidden fat.

phrases.english: Which is not so on שבת, where he is exempt.
As when he intended to lift something detached
and cut something attached: he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁגַג בְּלֹא מִתְכַּוֵּין, דְּקָסָבַר רוֹק הוּא וּבְלָעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the סיפא of the split reading proposed in step 14 with concrete cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case for the second half under the split reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שוגג בלא מתכוין would have to be found inside עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: שוגג בלא מתכוין is eating something forbidden thinking it was spittle, which is liable. The שבת parallel of cutting an attached plant while meaning to lift a detached one is פטור.

steps.title: שמואל's rule supports the difference between forbidden foods and שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the distinction from Step 15 matches a known rule of רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: a מתעסק is liable for forbidden fats and forbidden relations because he got pleasure, but is exempt on שבת because only planned labor is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: someone who accidentally eats forbidden fats or has forbidden relations, without meaning to do the act at all, is liable, because he got pleasure from it. But someone who does a מלאכה on שבת that way is exempt, because the Torah only forbids planned work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a known rule to show that the distinction it just made, liable for food but exempt for שבת, is well grounded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15 the גמרא said that swallowing forbidden food by accident makes a person liable, while cutting a plant by accident on שבת does not. Here it gives the reason. For eating and relations the pleasure itself makes him liable, but on שבת the Torah requires מלאכת מחשבת, work done on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who does a forbidden act without meaning to do that act at all
Forbidden animal fats
Forbidden sexual relations
Since he got pleasure from it
Planned, purposeful labor, the only kind the Torah forbids on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for all of הלכה: on שבת a מתעסק is exempt, but with forbidden pleasures he is still liable.

phrases.english: And this is like what Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel,
who said: one who acts unawares with forbidden fats or forbidden relations
is liable, since he got pleasure;
phrases.notes: Liable here means he must bring a חטאת for his mistake.

phrases.english: one who acts unawares on Shabbat is exempt,
because the Torah forbade planned labor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source and reason for the distinction made in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that שוגג בלא מתכוין is liable for forbidden foods but exempt on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: a מתעסק is liable for חלבים and עריות because of pleasure, and exempt on שבת because of מלאכת מחשבת

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן did not use this answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן did not accept the split reading because he never explains the first half of a ברייתא with one subject or reason and the second half with another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן follows his usual approach: he does not explain the beginning of a ברייתא one way and the end of it another way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a hidden question: if this split answer works so well, why didn't רבי יוחנן use it? The answer is that he rejects this kind of answer in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Steps 14-16 needed the ברייתא to switch topics in the middle, with the first half about עבודה זרה and the second half about other מצוות. רבי יוחנן has a general rule against splitting a teaching like that. So the answer is fine in itself, but it does not fit his method.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own known reasoning
Sets up or explains a source as referring to a certain case
The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the split answer is wrong. It only explains why רבי יוחנן personally would not use it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
since he does not explain a teaching

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the split reading from Steps 14-16 was not available to רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Methodological: the answer conflicts with the speaker's interpretive rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since splitting the ברייתא works, רבי יוחנן should have answered that way
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן never splits a ברייתא into two different reasons, so he could not use this answer

steps.title: The barrel statement proves רבי יוחנן's approach
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן said he would serve anyone who could explain the 'barrel' משנה according to a single תנא, which shows he does not accept splitting a teaching between two views.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: whoever can explain the משנה about the barrel according to one תנא, I will carry his clothes after him to the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי יוחנן himself to prove that he does not like splitting a teaching into two parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The barrel משנה looks like it holds two opinions, and רבי יוחנן said it can only be explained that way. He offered to be the servant of anyone who could explain it as one view, which shows how firmly he held to his method. That is the same method that blocked the split answer here.

keyTerms.meaning: Who explains
Barrel, the name for a certain משנה about a barrel
According to a single תנא
Bathhouse

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן does not explain a teaching as switching subjects or opinions in the middle. Because of this, the split reading of the ברייתא does not work for him.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whoever explains to me the barrel case
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about a barrel in בבא מציעא 40b.
